paragraphs.title: The Psalm’s Heading and Initial Confession

easy.explanation: David begins, “Have mercy upon me, O God, according to thy lovingkindness.”
easy.q: What does David ask God to do according to His lovingkindness?

easy.explanation: He asks God to “blot out” his transgressions.
easy.q: What does David ask God to blot out?

easy.explanation: David says, “Wash me throughly from mine iniquity.”
easy.q: What does David ask God to wash him from?

medium.explanation: The phrase presents God’s mercies as abundant and compassionate.
medium.q: What does the phrase “the multitude of thy tender mercies” emphasize?

answers: David seeks forgiveness through God’s compassionate cleansing
David asks to hide his sin from God
medium.explanation: David asks for mercy and then asks to be washed and cleansed from sin.
medium.q: How are mercy and cleansing connected in these verses?

medium.explanation: His requests show that he depends humbly on God’s mercy.
medium.q: What attitude does David show in his opening request?

answers: He recognizes that forgiveness depends on God’s mercy
He claims that he has never sinned
He wants to boast of his obedience
challenge.explanation: David bases his plea on God’s lovingkindness and tender mercies, not his own merit.
challenge.q: Why does David appeal to God’s lovingkindness rather than to his own merit?

answers: Mercy, blotting out transgressions, and cleansing from sin
challenge.explanation: David moves from asking for mercy to removal and cleansing of sin.
challenge.q: What progression appears in the opening requests?

answers: David is preparing for a journey
David is describing a public feast
challenge.explanation: The imagery expresses a desire to be thoroughly purified from sin.
challenge.q: What does the repeated language of washing and cleansing suggest?

paragraphs.title: A Plea for Mercy and Acceptance of Responsibility

easy.explanation: David says, “For I acknowledge my transgressions.”
He declares, “my sin is ever before me.”
easy.q: Where is David’s sin continually before him?

easy.explanation: David says, “Against thee, thee only, have I sinned.”
easy.q: Against whom does David say he has sinned?

answers: He accepts responsibility for his wrongdoing
He denies that he has sinned
He blames Nathan for his actions
medium.explanation: Acknowledging his transgressions shows that David accepts responsibility.
medium.q: What does David’s acknowledgment of sin show?

answers: God is justified and clear when He judges
medium.explanation: David says God is justified when He speaks and clear when He judges.
medium.q: What does David affirm about God’s judgment?

answers: Confidence that he needs no forgiveness
medium.explanation: The statement expresses David’s continuing awareness of his sin.
medium.q: What does “my sin is ever before me” communicate?

answers: David admits his sin and recognizes God’s justice
David confesses only to accuse God
David accepts no responsibility for his actions
challenge.explanation: David acknowledges his sin while affirming that God is right in judgment.
challenge.q: How do confession and acceptance of judgment work together in this passage?

answers: David identifies God as the ultimate one against whom he sinned
David says that no one else was affected by his actions
David denies that his conduct had earthly consequences
challenge.explanation: The phrase places David’s ultimate accountability before God.
challenge.q: What is the significance of the words “thee only”?

challenge.explanation: David says, “thou desirest truth in the inward parts.”
challenge.q: What does verse 6 say God desires in the inward parts?

easy.q: With what does David ask God to purge him?

easy.explanation: He says, “and I shall be clean.”
easy.q: What does David expect after being purged?

easy.explanation: God will make him know wisdom in the hidden part.
easy.q: What does David ask God to make him know?

medium.explanation: Being whiter than snow pictures thorough purification.
medium.q: What does the comparison to snow emphasize?

medium.explanation: David says God desires truth “in the inward parts.”
medium.q: Where does David say God desires truth?

medium.explanation: He asks God to make him hear “joy and gladness.”
medium.q: What does David ask to hear after cleansing?

answers: Repentance involves both honest self-knowledge and purification
Repentance requires only an outward ritual
Truth has no connection to cleansing
challenge.explanation: The passage joins inward truth, wisdom, and cleansing in David’s repentance.
challenge.q: What does the movement from inward truth to cleansing suggest?

answers: God’s restoration can bring joy after deep distress
David wants his suffering to continue forever
The image describes a military victory
challenge.explanation: David trusts that God can restore joy even after severe inner pain.
challenge.q: How does the image of broken bones relate to David’s hope for joy?

answers: It is meant to be thorough and unmistakable
It is merely symbolic of physical bathing
challenge.explanation: The comparison expresses a complete and visible purity.
challenge.q: What does the request to be whiter than snow imply about the desired cleansing?

paragraphs.title: Renewal of the Heart and Spirit

easy.explanation: David prays, “Create in me a clean heart, O God.”
easy.q: What does David ask God to create in him?

answers: Cast him away from His presence
easy.explanation: He says, “Cast me not away from thy presence.”
easy.q: What does David ask God not to do?

easy.explanation: David asks, “Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation.”
easy.q: What does David ask God to restore?

answers: A clean heart and a right spirit
A strong body and a rich house
A new altar and a new city
medium.explanation: He asks for a clean heart and for God to renew a right spirit within him.
medium.q: What two inner renewals does David request?

medium.explanation: David asks, “renew a right spirit within me.”
medium.q: What does David ask God to renew within him?

medium.explanation: He asks God to uphold him with His free spirit.
medium.q: What does David ask to support him?

answers: David seeks inward transformation, not only pardon
David wants to avoid admitting his sin
David asks for outward success without change
challenge.explanation: A clean heart shows that David seeks a transformed inner life.
challenge.q: What does the request for a created clean heart add to the request for forgiveness?

answers: Joy is presented as the result of restored fellowship with God
challenge.explanation: The order suggests that spiritual renewal leads to restored joy.
challenge.q: Why does joy appear after the requests for cleansing and renewal?

answers: David admits his guilt but still seeks continued fellowship with God
David wants to abandon God after forgiveness
challenge.explanation: David recognizes his sin while longing to remain in God’s presence.
challenge.q: What tension is expressed by asking not to be cast away while asking for a clean heart?

easy.explanation: David says, “Then will I teach transgressors thy ways.”
easy.q: Whom does David say he will teach?
What does David ask God to deliver him from?

answers: A broken and a contrite heart
easy.explanation: God will not despise “a broken and a contrite heart.”
easy.q: What kind of heart does God not despise?

answers: They shall be converted unto God
medium.explanation: David says, “sinners shall be converted unto thee.”
medium.q: What will happen to sinners when David teaches God’s ways?

medium.explanation: David says his tongue shall sing aloud of God’s righteousness.
medium.q: What does David’s tongue say it will do after deliverance?

medium.explanation: He prays, “O Lord, open thou my lips.”
medium.q: What does David ask God to open?

answers: His restored testimony can teach them God’s ways
His restoration prevents him from speaking
His restoration makes repentance unnecessary for others
challenge.explanation: David expects his restored life and testimony to guide sinners toward God.
challenge.q: How can David’s personal restoration affect other sinners?

answers: God values a broken and contrite heart rather than empty ritual
God rejects every form of worship
God values sacrifices regardless of the heart
challenge.explanation: The passage presents the broken spirit and contrite heart as the sacrifice God will not despise.
challenge.q: What contrast does the passage make between sacrifice and the broken spirit?

answers: A forgiven person can openly praise God and testify to His righteousness
The lips are opened only for political speech
The request is meant to hide David’s guilt
challenge.explanation: David wants his opened mouth to declare God’s praise and righteousness.
challenge.q: How do opened lips relate to repentance?

easy.explanation: David prays, “Do good in thy good pleasure unto Zion.”
easy.q: For whose good does David ask God to do good?

easy.explanation: He asks, “build thou the walls of Jerusalem.”
easy.q: What does David ask God to build?

easy.explanation: The passage says God will be pleased with “the sacrifices of righteousness.”
easy.q: What kind of sacrifices will please God?

answers: His concern extends from personal restoration to the community
He no longer cares about repentance
He wants to replace worship with warfare
medium.explanation: David ends by praying for the good of Zion and Jerusalem.
medium.q: What does the request for Jerusalem show about David’s concern?

answers: Burnt offering and whole burnt offering
medium.explanation: The verse mentions burnt offering and whole burnt offering.
medium.q: What offerings are mentioned along with sacrifices of righteousness?

answers: Good for Zion, rebuilding Jerusalem, and acceptable sacrifices
medium.explanation: The closing movement goes from Zion’s good to Jerusalem’s walls and then righteous sacrifices.
medium.q: What is the sequence in the closing passage?

answers: True repentance can include concern for the welfare of the wider community
Personal sin never affects anyone else
David abandons his request for mercy
challenge.explanation: The conclusion broadens David’s prayer from personal forgiveness to communal restoration.
challenge.q: What does the shift from personal confession to Zion suggest?

answers: The acceptable sacrifices are connected with righteousness and a rightly restored life
The sacrifices replace the need for repentance
The final sacrifices are unrelated to the heart
challenge.explanation: The closing sacrifices are acceptable within the context of righteousness and repentance.
challenge.q: How are the sacrifices in the final verse related to the earlier broken heart?

answers: Restoration depends on God’s gracious will
Restoration is earned by military strength
challenge.explanation: David asks God to act according to His good pleasure and favor.
challenge.q: What does “in thy good pleasure” emphasize about Jerusalem’s restoration?
